RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel composition tells you nothing useful here: you're a man who lost to a man. An all-male panel can't plausibly have favoured a man over you on the basis of sex, and raising it would look like grasping, undermining the parts of your case that are actually strong.

What's strong: a two-week silence on a reasonable request for written reasons, and a successful candidate with roughly half your experience and a vaguer-sounding rationale ("excellent client relationships"). Chase the explanation in writing, note the date of your original request, and ask specifically how the criteria were weighted.

The real question may be favouritism or an undisclosed internal preference — not sex.
